about: LIN-3172: the 25 supervisor failures on record (what-supervisors-do.md v2, as corrected by survey-check-2.md: the 26 of what-supervisors-do-failures.json less LIN-1884, LIN-2899, LIN-1591, LIN-2754, LIN-2229 and LIN-2468, plus LIN-353, LIN-430, LIN-870, LIN-1280 and LIN-1451), each placed on the wake-inventory path it failed on, by hand, from each ticket's title and description (read over the workspace proxy for the five added ones on 2026-09-30). path: the inventory row in wake-inventory.md (H = Harbour, S = simple-dispatcher), or 'dispatch' / 'landing' where the failure is in what a supervisor dispatched or merged rather than in a wake. effect: lost (a wake owed and not delivered, or delivered and then destroyed), duplicated (one event, two wakes or a loop), misdelivered (delivered with the wrong content), or none (not a wake failure).

failures.why: recommend-and-dispatch's container descent re-descended to a Done child and looped; a routing decision, not a wake
the recommend engine kept choosing investigate; a routing decision
descent did not defer an epic to its ready child
an autopilot merged two red-CI PRs; the landing gate, not a wake
a woken session zombied instead of resuming or terminating after the follow-up was signalled into its hold
stepper beats carried the hold but not the everything subscription, so [pending] never woke the head
a follow-up itemId repoint severed the edge the terminal wake resolves through
an up-chain wake self-looped into the producing session
the Stop hook's re-entry guard swallowed the completion gate's sentinel

two orchestrators dispatched the same issue and kind minutes apart
the stall failsafe killed a correctly standing-by subscribed parent
a wake lost on the cold-resume launch path was never re-delivered

an abort row and the aborted child's row each minted a terminal wake
